subject.title: improve(ci): retain Node 22 declaration cache across runs

question: Should this low-impact CI optimization land with a controlled post-merge cold-save/warm-restore verification, or wait for equivalent trusted cross-run proof before merge?
rationale: The workflow intentionally prevents the PR branch from acting as an accepted producer, so exact real-behavior proof cannot be generated through the normal branch run; accepting a post-merge verification window requires explicit maintainer ownership.

options.title: Controlled post-merge verification
options.body: Merge with the existing cold fallback, capture publication and subsequent restore logs on `main`, and revert if the artifact path fails.

options.title: Require trusted staging proof
options.body: Pause until an equivalent trusted repository or maintainer-controlled workflow demonstrates the exact cross-run artifact lifecycle before merge.

recommendation.title: Controlled post-merge verification
recommendation.body: Merge with the existing cold fallback, capture publication and subsequent restore logs on `main`, and revert if the artifact path fails.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the declaration-reuse behavior, authored its persistence follow-up, and are assigned to the PR.
